questions.q: Ramlal marks up his goods by 40% and gives a discount of 10%. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For successive percentage changes, use the net effect formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (a) = +40% and Discount (b) = −10%

Net Profit % = 40 − 10 + [40 × (−10)] ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 30 − 4 = 26%

∴ The correct answer is 26%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup Percentage = 40%

Discount Percentage = 10%

Formula Used:

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100



Calculations:

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + (40% of 100) = 140

⇒ Discount given = 10% on MP = (10 ÷ 100) × 140 = 14

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 140 − 14 = 126

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 126 − 100 = 26

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (26 ÷ 100) × 100 = 26%

∴ The correct answer is 26%.

Additional Information

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Marked Price (MP) is always calculated by applying the markup percentage on the Cost Price (CP). Formula: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net effective change is given by the formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (MP), never on the Cost Price. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Direct CP to MP Ratio

The direct relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by the ratio: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Does Sneha not lick the butter?
options: Is the butter being licked by Sneha?
Is the butter not licked by Sneha?
Sneha does not lick the butter?
Was Sneha not licking the butter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Is the butter not licked by Sneha?'

Key Points

• The given sentence is written in an interrogative form as the question tag is there, and we need to convert it into the passive form.

• Active Voice describes a sentence where the subject performs the action stated by the verb. While in the Passive Voice subject is acted upon by the verb.

• We follow the following structure in case of an interrogative sentence:

• Active voice: Do/Does/Did + Doer + Verb 1 + Noun/Pronoun + Rest of the sentence

• Example - *Do they beat you every day? (Active)*

• Passive voice: Am/is/are/was/were + Noun/Pronoun + Verb 3 + By + Doer + Rest of the sentence

• Example - *Are you beaten by them every day? (Passive)*

• While converting Interrogative Active into Interrogative Passive Voice.

• The helping verb comes before the object in the passive voice, (as the passive voice starts with the object of the active voice)

• Convert the verb into past participle or 3rd form of the verb.

• Use the preposition ‘by’.

• Complete the sentence with the subject and sign of Interrogation (?).

• Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.

Correct Passive form: *Is the butter not licked by Sneha?*
